claims.claim: A volcano is a vent through which molten rock and other materials reach Earth's surface, together with the landform built around the vent.
Magma is molten rock beneath Earth's surface; lava is the same material after it reaches the surface.

Shield volcanoes are broad and gently sloping because fluid lava flows spread far from the vent; composite (stratovolcano) volcanoes are tall and steep-sided, built of alternating lava and fragmental layers; cinder cones are small, steep-sided hills of loose ejected fragments.

About 1,350 potentially active volcanoes exist on land (excluding the ocean floor), about 500 of which have erupted in historical time; Mauna Loa is the largest active volcano on Earth, and Kīlauea erupted almost continuously from 1983 for decades.
Volcanoes occur at convergent boundaries (Ring of Fire), divergent boundaries, and above hotspots such as Hawai'i and Yellowstone.

Magma viscosity and dissolved gas content shape eruption style: fluid basaltic magma produces shields and lava flows, while viscous, gas-rich magma (e.g., the dacite of Mount St. Helens) favors explosive eruptions and steep composite edifices.

Pyroclastic flows typically travel faster than 80 km/h at temperatures of 200-700 °C; lahars can exceed 200 km/h and grow to more than ten times their original size; basaltic lava flows typically move slower than 1 km/h, up to about 10 km/h on steep slopes, and faster in channels; ash particles are smaller than 2 mm.
Water vapor is the most abundant volcanic gas, and volcanoes worldwide emit an estimated 180 to 440 million tonnes of carbon dioxide per year.
Volcano monitoring combines seismicity, ground deformation, gas emissions, water chemistry, and satellite observations.

On May 18, 1980, a magnitude 5.1 earthquake at 8:32 a.m. triggered the Mount St. Helens lateral blast, which moved at least 480 km/h, devastated about 600 km², released about 540 million tons of ash, and lowered the summit by about 400 m to its current elevation of about 2,539 m (8,330 ft); Mount St. Helens is a stratovolcano built of dacite.
